mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 5% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO YoY < -2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in the last quarter
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises and payroll employment (PAYEMS) falls simultaneously over a month, it signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases simultaneously and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter, it signals increased borrowing costs, which typically lead to reduced corporate investment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% in a quarter and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances over a 3-year period.
